articles.title: Investors sue chip giant Intel after 29% stock plunge
articles.description: A proposed class action says Intel hid the impact of slowing sales, inflating its shares.
articles.summary: Shareholders have sued US chip giant Intel, accusing it of hiding the severity of a slump in personal computer (PC) sales, which they say led to a nearly 29% one-day collapse in the firm's stock.
key_points: A proposed class action lawsuit in San Jose, California said Intel was too late to alert shareholders about how slowing sales could impact its earnings, allegedly artificially inflating its stock price.
Intel shares plunged on 30 October, erasing tens of billions of dollars off its market value the day after it forecasted disappointing revenue in its coming earnings report.
The lawsuit, filed by legal firm Robbins Geller Rudman & Dowd on behalf of owners of Intel common shares between 23 July and 29 October this year, was filed against the chipmaker, its…

articles.title: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
articles.description: The Nvidia scandal has raised questions over whether advanced AI chips ended up in China, despite US restrictions.
articles.summary: The Nvidia scandal has sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley as well as the political establishment Alice Huang, a suspected China spy who has been linked to Nvidia's former boss Jensen Huang, left her executive role at Megaspeed in August last year, the company says.
key_points: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of the AI chip-making giant Nvidia after it emerged he had allegedly had affairs with Alice Huang as well as with one of his employees.
Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in south-east Asia and the scandal at Nvidia has raised questions about the possibility that high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite…
The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.

articles.title: Black Friday and tax return scams - don't fall for these
articles.description: Tens of thousands of scams are reported to HMRC - so it has advice on how to spot a fake request and refund.
articles.summary: This month's Black Friday and the tax return deadline at the end of January are both opportunities for fraudsters to scam you.
key_points: That's because people are more likely to expect emails, texts and other correspondence at this time of year.
Fraudsters will use the dates to impersonate genuine organisations and retailers by pushing victims towards fake websites to steal personal information.
Here's how to spot a scam and how you can avoid being caught out.

articles.title: Cut National Insurance for under-25s to create jobs, Milburn report to say
articles.description: The report being launched this week will suggest gradually reducing employment costs over five years.
articles.summary: Alan Milburn's report will also make recommendations on cutting the benefits bill National Insurance (NI) paid by businesses on workers aged under 25 should be gradually lowered to encourage companies to create jobs for young people, a major review of youth unemployment will say.
key_points: A report by former Labour minister Alan Milburn will suggest the government should reduce NI costs over five years for people aged between 21 and 24 years old, starting in retail and hospitality.
Under Sir Keir Starmer, the government raised NI for firms.
Milburn will say the number of young people not in employment, education or training - known as Neets - was not started by the NI rise.

articles.title: UK will have 'voice' but no vote on EU food rules in Brexit reset
articles.description: EU minister Hamish Falconer insists Britain would have some influence on policy as part of a new deal.
articles.summary: The UK will have a "voice in the room" but no vote on European Union food policies as part of a so-called "Brexit reset" to reduce red tape, EU relations minister Hamish Falconer has told the BBC.
key_points: Prime Minister Andy Burnham hopes to agree a deal at a summit on Friday but critics have said a reset will make the UK "a rule taker" but not a rule maker.
Falconer said the UK will be involved in a process to shape the rules and said the deal could help bring down prices for shoppers.
The reset would not involve any upfront payments, Falconer added, but made it clear there could well be an "exit clause" in case a future UK government reversed the closer alignment.

articles.title: Minister backs legal right to job support for young people
articles.description: The work and pensions secretary said the level of support currently on offer was too vague.
articles.summary: Watch: Pat McFadden refuses to rule out that some young people might lose benefits The work and pensions secretary has backed the idea that the government should legally guarantee young people help to get into employment.
key_points: Pat McFadden told the BBC that job support should be given a "legislative underpinning", adding the level of assistance on offer was currently "vague".
McFadden also confirmed that some current benefit claimants would see their current entitlement to benefits reduced when they are reassessed.
But his Conservative counterpart Helen Whately said the idea of legally guaranteeing support "doesn't make sense" and ministers should focus instead on reducing taxes paid by employers.

articles.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after day-long global outage
articles.description: Efforts to address the underlying problem with Outlook, Teams and Copilot are complete, the tech firm says.
articles.summary: Products such as Microsoft Teams and Outlook have been out of service for much of Friday Microsoft has said its services have been fully restored after a worldwide outage affected several of its tools, causing disruption.
key_points: The tech firm said early on Saturday morning that efforts to address the underlying problem had been completed and customers using Outlook, Teams and Copilot should no longer be affected.
The outage hit more than 70 countries, disrupting everything from business operations to government services and personal users.
More than 430 million people use the affected products worldwide.

articles.title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
articles.description: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.
articles.summary: A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.
key_points: On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair.
He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips.
For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets.

articles.title: Pressure grows on Trump's Commerce Secretary Lutnick in fallout from Nvidia scandal
articles.description: Scott Bessent told CNBC that several government agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".
articles.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed Howard Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-spec AI chips, as the fallout from the Nvidia scandal widens to President Donald Trump's cabinet.
key_points: Pressure is building on Lutnick from across the political spectrum to explain his department's actions.
Jensen Huang was ousted as Nvidia CEO after revelations he had an affair with a businesswoman who was also allegedly a Chinese spy.
Megaspeed, the firm she worked for, had been probed by US government agencies over suspicions it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China, reports said, but it is not on a list of firms…

articles.title: Why is Microsoft's outage lasting so long and will emails be lost?
articles.description: Microsoft says it is continuing to restore services including Outlook and Teams following a global outage.
articles.summary: A major Microsoft outage has impacted schools, healthcare systems, businesses, courts and governments around the world.
key_points: Services including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot, are being restored almost 24 hours since issues first surfaced.
Microsoft said the outage was not a cyber-security incident and was caused by a technical issue.
Here's what we know about the services affected and what went wrong.

articles.title: Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy
articles.description: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs.
articles.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been summoned to testify next month before a Senate committee about his alleged affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy.
key_points: Huang abruptly quit on Thursday as head of one of the world's most valuable companies after revelations of alleged extramarital affairs, in a stunning fall from grace that sent shockwaves through Silicon Valley.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December.
Nvidia has lost $550bn (£415bn) in stock market value in just five days as the scandal dominated headlines.

articles.title: Burnham says 'win-win' deal can be agreed between UK and EU
articles.description: The prime minister says the deal could be "more like the Brexit people thought they were voting for" in 2016.
articles.summary: Andy Burnham said he believes a "win-win" deal can be agreed with the European Union, adding it could be "more like the Brexit that people thought they were voting for" in 2016.
key_points: The prime minister is exploring closer ties with the bloc and is expected to sign new agreements on food, energy and youth mobility at a UK-EU summit on 20 November.
Speaking after meeting European leaders in Ireland on Thursday, Burnham said he hopes a deal could help lower prices and boost the UK economy.
He predicted the negotiations could "go down to the wire".
